correctness.rationale: The full target-slice count follows by five field-generic steps. Trace pairing forces the two sl2 inputs into the upper triangular subalgebra and gives exactly q(q^2-1) ordered pairs for [X,Y]=e. Each Heisenberg block then has a rank-two affine solution space. A nonzero y-target coefficient makes the central output uniform via a kernel translation; when all y-targets vanish, the explicitly verified inner symplectic shear removes the x-targets, leaving q^n free variables times the exact number of solutions to a nondegenerate n-square equation. Quadratic Gauss sums prove the character formulas and both three-level multiplicity tables. Direct bracket-equation enumeration independently checks all targets and zero fibers over (q,n)=(3,1),(3,2),(3,3),(5,1),(5,2),(7,1). The all-prime-power proof is symbolic, not an extrapolation from these tests.

value.rationale: The motivating bracket-width theorem makes the occurrence of e+cz a concrete gap. The result solves a natural ordered-witness count on the full nilpotent-output slice for every n and every odd finite field, not a single ad hoc matrix parameter. The uniform/character-dependent dichotomy gives sharp output multiplicities and identifies all noncommutator targets at n=1 while showing universal positivity for n>=2. The three-level spectrum also quantifies heterogeneity that qualitative bracket width and the previous zero/central-target counts cannot detect.
